# The projection

Where a number lands by its due week if the recent trend holds: the likeliest value and a range around it.

## The rule

The projection fits a least-squares line through the recent numbers, not a slope between two points, so one noisy week can't swing it.

**The numbers it uses** (a *series* of week and value, oldest first; see “Where it is used” for which points):

- *last* is the latest point. Take the points with week > *last*.week − 8 (the last 8 weeks).
- If those span fewer than 3 weeks (*last*.week − first week < 3), reach back to the latest point at least 3 weeks before *last*, and use it and every point after it. If there is none, there is **no projection** (`null`): it needs a number at least three weeks before the latest one.

**The line.** With *n* points, *x̄* and *ȳ* the mean week and value, *Sxx* = Σ(*x* − *x̄*)², *slope* = Σ(*x* − *x̄*)(*y* − *ȳ*) / *Sxx*:

- *spread* = √(Σ(*y* − line)² / (*n* − 2)) when *n* > 2, else 0.
- A slope the numbers barely support counts for little: *t* = *slope* / (*spread* / √*Sxx*) (infinite when the spread is 0), and the line leans by *lean* = *t*² / (1 + *t*²) (1 when *t* is infinite).
- To week *T*: *value* = *ȳ* + *lean* · *slope* · (*T* − *x̄*).
- *half* = *spread* · √(1/*n* + (*T* − *x̄*)² / *Sxx*); *low* = *value* − *half*, *high* = *value* + *half*. About two chances in three that the number lands inside if nothing changes. A clean trend has no spread, so its range is the line itself.
- Every result (value, low, high, slope) is rounded to 9 decimal places. The *slope* it gives is the one the line leans by, *lean* · *slope*, not the fitted slope (the conformance data's `slope` column is this one). It also says *from* (first week used), *to* (*last*.week) and *week* (*T*).

**Held to what the number can be** (`projectionFor`, which every projection of a goal's own numbers goes through), judged on the goal as it is projected: a number to move with the plan as of the week judged (its start, its target and its hand-set points; earlier plans in `planHistory` don't count), a range with its limit alone (no start or target).

- A *share* (`isShare`): the unit, trimmed, is `%`, and every one of those plan numbers is within 0–100. Value, low and high are held to 0–100.
- A *count* (`isCount`): 0 decimals; every one of those plan numbers a whole number, zero or more; and a unit that, trimmed and in lower case, is not `%` and doesn't match `/^(days?|hours?|hrs?|mins?|minutes?|weeks?|secs?|seconds?|ms|pts?|points?|score|nps)$|usd|gbp|eur|\$|£|€|°/` (a time, money, points or a score: the whole unit is one of those words, or it holds a currency code or sign or a degree sign anywhere). Value, low and high are held at or above 0. The unit is otherwise free: `deploys`, `templates`, `TB` and `checks` are counts when the rest holds.

**Where it is used.** A number to move projects to its due week (`endWeek` of the plan as of the week judged, the latest check-in's; else the cycle's end) from every earlier check-in that has a number (all of them, in week order then posting order, even two in one week) plus the number of the week judged. A range goal's scorecard projects to the cycle's end from one number per week (the latest posted in each week wins).

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Numbers in weeks 1 and 2 only, projected to week 13. | `none` |
| 10 in week 1 and 16 in week 4, to week 13. | `value 34, range 34–34, slope 2` |
| A clean trend: 0 in week 1, 10 in week 3, 25 in week 6, to week 13. | `value 60, range 60–60, slope 5` |
| An old slump doesn’t count: 90 in week 1, 10 in week 2, then 20, 22, … 34 in weeks 10–17, to week 20. | `from week 10, value 40` |
| A noisy CSAT: 84, 81, 86, 82, 87, 80, 85, 83, 84, 81, 86, 82 in weeks 34–45, to week 53. | `value 83.096, range 78.397–87.796, from week 38` |
| Incidents, a count: 12, 8, 3, 2 in weeks 1, 3, 5, 6, to week 13. The bare line goes below zero; the goal’s projection stops at 0. | `line low -14.33; held: value 0, low 0` |
| The latest check-in of each week counts: week 2 posted twice (5, then 7 a day later), and week 1 with 3. | `1: 3, 2: 7` |
| The same noisy CSAT: the slope the line was fitted with, and the slope the projection gives (leaned). | `fitted -0.19, given -0.035` |
| Whole-number goals from 0 to 10 in deploys, ms, USD, pts, TB and min; then deploys from 0 to 10.5 with 1 decimal; then % from 10 to 40. | `count, not, not, not, count, not; not; share` |
| The 30→75 goal with 42 in week 3 and 45 in week 6: the likeliest value at week 13, and whether it misses the target. | `52, misses` |

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/plan.ts](../../../src/domain/plan.ts): `projection`, `projectionFor`, `isShare`, `isCount`, `valueSeries`, `PROJECTION_WEEKS`

## Requirements

- `FORECAST`: The projection is a least-squares line through the last eight weeks of numbers (reaching back to one three weeks earlier when they're sparse), leaning only as far as the numbers support, projected to the due week as a range, and only shown with enough data.
- `PROJECTION-RANGE`: The projection is steady on a noisy number and called exactly on a clean trend: one more noisy week moves it by a few points, not tens; it is a range everywhere it's shown (the chart, Home and reviews' warnings, exports and the AI assistant's get_goal).

## Tests that check it

### [src/domain/rules.test.ts](../../../src/domain/rules.test.ts)

- plan › counts weeks from the start date
- plan › shapes the plan: straight, back-loaded (w/13)^1.5, three steps
- plan › projects from a line through the recent weeks, and needs three weeks of numbers
- plan › is steady on a noisy number: a range, not a swing from one week (the support example’s CSAT)
- plan › never projects a count below zero, or a share outside 0–100%
- plan › keeps the latest check-in for each week

### [src/domain/scorecard.test.ts](../../../src/domain/scorecard.test.ts)

- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › likely when the target sits comfortably on the near side of the likeliest value, or below the whole range
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › possible when the target is close to the likeliest value or inside the range on its better side
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › unlikely when the target is beyond the range by up to half its width; very unlikely further
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › reads the same way round when lower is better
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › a clean trend with no spread still has a little doubt, from the floor
- amounts say their unit once, in the singular for one › hours, days and points
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a number goal, lower is better: vs plan, vs last week, to target, and will it hit
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a skipped week: the sub-line names the week compared
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a goal gone quiet says nothing about where it lands
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a stopped goal says how it stood and makes no forecast: no “will it hit?”, no likely end on the chart
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a range: vs the limit, vs last week, room to the limit, and will it stay within
- the scorecard on the example › lead time for changes: behind plan and very unlikely to reach 24 hours
- the scorecard on the example › dated stages: done, late, and the next one due
- the scorecard on the example › every goal gets a card that never says a percentage chance
